eventRemarks: Cold, cloudy, light south-easterly breeze, around 12 degrees Celsius----The resident male Blue-billed Duck was diving to feed about 15m south-south-west of the viewing area in the north-west of the lake, watching two female Hardhead about 6 and 8m to his east. He dove under and I took pics of the two Hardhead, when he arose he paddled off to the south-west corner with a brief westerly diversion to avoid a Pacific Black Duck paddling in towards the viewing area. I took pictures of the other lake birds, noting the Black Swan pair who have been on the lake for just over a month dipping to feed on Eel Grass in the south-east lake corner, and there were six Hardhead Ducks - two males and 4 females paddling about, preening, brief diving to feed. The male Blue-billed Duck seemed to paddle out from the spare reeds on the western end of the southern bank, paddling directly towards the viewing area for some close pics. He turned east about 6m out from the rocky overflow area, briefly avoiding some dipping Eurasian Coot who were moving slowly west. He dove to feed in a thick Eel Grass patch close to the bank about 4m out and I lost track of him, probably moving out of view below the bank and moving into the hidden north-east to keep diving in a hollow - he's been living on the lake for coming up to a year now, a comfortable home, waiting for females to fly in looking for nesting sites.4

eventRemarks: Cold, cloudy with passing showers, around 14 degrees----At the viewing area in the north-west and a pair of Black Swans were at the rocky overflow area into Blind Creek. The larger of the pair I assume was the male hooted loudly and clambered awkwardly over the rocks towards the fence, stopping halfway to eat from a loose pile of Eel Grass that had been blown in by the southerly breeze, his smaller female partner following behind. Looking to the south-east, about 10m out, curled up in his normal napping spot, was the resident male Blue-billed duck, living on the lake for many months - his body point south-east, bill over his left shoulder, tucked under the top of his right wing, eyes firmly closed, stiff tail feathers slightly fanned at 45 degrees. His favourite napping spot. I took pics and made a count for this checklist as the Swan pair paddled out into the north-west area to dip for more Eel Grass. Towards the end of the  brief  session, the male Blue-billed Duck woke up, looked towards the central-north hollow in front of the bank, did some stretches and preening, then paddled into the area to dive to feed. The had been a younger male Blue-billed duck here for about a month and a half, seeming to be friends with the resident male, however it seems he may have flown away in the last couple of days.
